title: What If the Biggest Solar Storm on Record Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if the biggest solar storm on record hit today? In 1859 it made telegraph wires throw sparks.
Today the weak link is the power grid. Lloyd's of London estimates twenty to forty million Americans could lose power.
A far weaker storm in 1989 blacked out Quebec in about ninety seconds.
Outages could last from several weeks to one or two years if giant transformers are permanently damaged.
Lloyd's puts the losses between six hundred billion and two point six trillion dollars.
Storms that big come roughly once in a hundred and fifty years. The last one was in 1859.
